genZNote: The bacterium behind 'Bt corn' and organic-approved insect sprays — it makes a crystal toxin that's lethal to caterpillars but harmless to us.

morphology.notes: Produces a parasporal crystalline protein inclusion (Cry/delta-endotoxin) alongside its endospore, visible as a distinctive crystal under the microscope.

habitat.hostAssociation: Not a human commensal or pathogen; insect-pathogenic in its target hosts
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Common soil bacterium worldwide; also formulated commercially as a biological insecticide

microscopy.appearance: Gram-positive rods with oval endospores and a distinct parasporal crystal

culture.growthCharacteristics: Aerobic/facultative growth, forms spores under nutrient limitation
culture.colonyMorphology: Large, flat, spreading, dull-white colonies resembling B. cereus

identificationClues: Genetically and phenotypically very close to Bacillus cereus, distinguished mainly by the parasporal crystal toxin it produces alongside its spore
The Cry (crystal) delta-endotoxin is specifically insecticidal, disrupting the gut lining of susceptible insect larvae after ingestion
Widely used as an organic-approved insecticide spray and as the source of Cry genes engineered into 'Bt' crops
Not considered a human pathogen under normal exposure, unlike its close relative B. cereus

examFacts.keyBiochemicalReaction: Catalase positive; produces parasporal crystal (Cry toxin)
examFacts.importantDisease: None in humans — insect pathogen used as a biopesticide
examFacts.importantTest: Microscopic visualization of the parasporal crystal alongside the spore
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Very close relative of B. cereus that makes an insecticidal crystal toxin, the basis of organic pest control and Bt-engineered crops

sources.name: NCBI Bookshelf — overview of Bacillus cereus group biology and Cry toxins
